text:
maria: Quick heads-up — experimenting with a compact pricing experience for launch next week. want to iterate FAQ microcopy, tier names, and the calculator UX. goal: reduce inbound questions and increase trial starts from the pricing page :sparkles:
josh: love it. what parts of the FAQ are highest priority? any data from recentsupport tickets? :eyes:
maria: top asks are around "commitment levels" and "burst capacity" — people confuse reserved capacity vs metered. want a short Q + 1-sentence answer approach. also trying 2 alternate tier name sets (functional vs benefit-led).
lee: can we try: Set A (Core / Scale / Enterprise) and Set B (Starter / Predictable / Mission)? lean toward Set B for clarity but open to test.
sam: Calculator UX idea: default to a simple monthly slider with a toggle for "Committed vs Pay as you go". show a small line: "Estimated monthly cost — includes batching discounts". maybe hide advanced options behind "Show details".
nina: inbound lead routing: if calculator results > $5k commit, route to enterprise SDR queue. otherwise route to marketing follow-up. also add UTM capture for webinar registrants to map conversions.
josh: ok routing rules sound good. for the webinar cohort we should add a special nurture sequence — "benchmark narrative" content that shows latency & cost vs common alternatives. do we have fresh numbers?
maria: Research has new bench numbers for the 4k token use case vs competitor X — 35% lower cost with similar latency on our Dedicated config. want to reference this in the benchmark blurb but keep it non-technical: "Lower per-unit cost at higher throughput" + link to detailed appendix.
lee: Draft for launch post headline: "Faster, predictable inference — new pricing to match real production needs". then 3 bullets: clear tiers, live calculator, benchmark snapshot.
sam: Wire copy for FAQ entry: Q: "How do commitments affect billing?" A: "Committed plans give you predictable monthly costs and priority capacity; usage beyond your commitment is billed at pay-as-you-go rates." short and actionable. add a tooltip for "priority capacity" linking to a glossary.
maria: also test microcopy variants on CTA: "Estimate my cost" vs "See my price". small wording change can impact conversion.
nina: tagging for analytics: set event name `pricing_calc_result` and include `commitment_level`, `estimated_monthly`, `utm_campaign`. ensure the enterprise routing rule checks `estimated_monthly >= 5000`.
josh: timeline — we need copy + mock by Tue, engineering can wire the slider Wed, and QA Thurs. webinar cohort email needs to be ready Fri.
lee: quick check: does marketing want the benchmark deck for the webinar? i'll update slides with charts (latency vs tokens, cost per 1k tokens).
maria: yes please. keep chart axis simplified and call out the 35% number. add a note: "Tested on Dedicated v2, 4k seq" in appendix.
sam: ui note: when user toggles "Committed" show a small inline example: "Commit $X/month -> Y throughput". helps reduce cognitive load.
josh: A/B testing plan: split 50/50 on CTA microcopy and tier names. track conversion to trial and inbound leads > $5k. run for 2 weeks.
maria: perfect. last thing — launch-bot scheduling: can you create a post in #general on day-of with the benchmark snapshot and link to pricing? launch-bot: scheduled post created for 2024-09-12 10:00 UTC.
nina: posting reminder: update the privacy blurb for EU — need EU pricing locale line.
lee: noted. i'll add localized currency toggle to the calculator mock.
josh: ok, next sync tomorrow 11am PT. cheers everyone :wave:
